target.title: fix(qa-channel): honor canonical thread action fields
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA channel users running thread actions through the shared message runner would lose a requested thread name, while thread replies and edits would fail validation despite supplying the canonical message-tool fields.

The runner normalizes destinations to `target`/`to`, thread names to `threadName`, and message bodies to `message`. The QA channel adapter still read its older private field names, so a create silently fell back to `QA thread`, and reply/edit stopped before reaching the QA bus.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QA channel now consumes the same canonical `target`, `threadName`, and `message` contract exposed by the CLI and message tool. Thread creation and replies also resolve the canonical target through the existing QA target parser and retain the QA bus's channel-only thread model.

The stale `title` schema contribution was removed. Runner-level coverage lives with the shared runner and assembles the bundled QA channel and QA bus only through their top-level public barrels, while adapter-level coverage remains inside the plugin boundary.

## User Impact

QA scenarios and operators can create named threads, reply within the returned thread target, and edit thread messages through the normal message action path. The QA bus receives the requested names and message bodies instead of defaults or missing-field errors.

## Evidence

- Before: canonical `threadName` produced the default `QA thread`; canonical thread reply and edit requests were rejected because the adapter looked for `channelId`/`text`.
- After: a real `runMessageAction` -> QA channel -> QA bus flow preserves the requested thread name, returned thread target, reply body/thread id, edit body, and final bus state.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.qa-channel.test.ts` (2 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-channel/src/channel.test.ts -t 'exposes thread and message actions'` (1 passed, 19 skipped)
- `node scripts/check-src-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json` (`[]`)
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files.
- Two independent Codex adversarial reviews checked the full handler, runner normalization, CLI/tool schema, public plugin boundary, QA bus contract, sibling actions, and tests. The first review found and drove the stale-schema and test-owner fixes; the second matched diff hash `c8ac7819e2ceeb2ba5c13c5b16d47635cf237105837d3b3975afd81560c1fe9d` and returned GO with no actionable findings.

AI-assisted: Codex was used for implementation, contract tracing, tests, and adversarial review. I reviewed the resulting behavior and understand the change.
